summary: US-A2: A signed-in purchase belongs to the account
description:
**As** a signed-in buyer, **I want** my purchase attached to my account at the moment I make it,
**so that** I never have to quote an order reference to find it again.

**Priority:** P0  **Depends on:** TKT-220

This is the slice that makes an account worth having, and it is the one that touches the **checkout
path** - so it is also the slice where a mistake is expensive. The rule it must not break: a guest
checkout stays byte-for-byte what it is today.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] `orders` gains a **nullable** customer reference. NULL means guest, guest stays the default,
  and nothing is backfilled. The column is nullable *because* the guest path is first-class, not as
  a migration convenience - say so in the migration comment.
- [ ] Checkout attributes the order to the authenticated customer. **The plan states how the caller
  proves it is that customer** and why that proof cannot be forged by a caller who simply names
  someone else's id. Attribution to a customer the caller has not authenticated as is **refused** -
  with a test that attempts exactly that.
- [ ] A **guest checkout is unchanged**: same request shape (no new required field), same response,
  same status codes, same recovery behaviour. A test pins that the guest path still stores NULL.
- [ ] The attribution does not perturb ADR-016's recovery states: `orders.status` gains no new value
  and `refunded` keeps meaning what it means (a compensated FAILED checkout).
- [ ] The order read exposes the attribution (contract-declared; regen committed).
- [ ] Replay/idempotency: re-submitting the same checkout with the same Idempotency-Key does not
  change or duplicate the attribution.
- [ ] Browser-submit verification (AGENTS.md): `make up`, then **submit** the new form(s) in a real browser — the smoke suite only renders, so the whole SSR-rejects-the-write class (origin check, base path, redirect, CSP) is invisible to it. Evidence in the PR. (buy while signed in, and buy while signed out.)
- [ ] `make check` green (lint + test + build, Go & TS, gateway smoke suite); regenerated code (`openapi_gen.go`, `api-types.gen.ts`) committed BEFORE the gate runs (ADR-009).

**Non-goals:** listing a customer's orders (TKT-222) - claiming a past guest order (TKT-223) -
purchase limits keyed on the customer (TKT-20) - transfers (TKT-9/TKT-160).

objective.note: An order made while signed in carries a stable customer identity; a guest order still carries none.

scope.note: One nullable column, one attribution path through checkout, one contract field. No read surface.

uncertainties.note: How the storefront proves the customer to commerce - session token exchanged for an assertion, a signed value, or a storefront-held credential. The ACs require the answer to be stated and to be unforgeable by a caller naming another id; the choice depends on TKT-220's ADR.

dependencies.note: Blocked by TKT-220 - there is no customer to attribute to until it lands.

approach.note: Follow the existing checkout write in services/commerce/internal/store/store.go, which already sets guest_order_ref under the same row lock. Attribution belongs in that same transaction, not a second write.

first_slice.note: Attributing at purchase time is strictly simpler than reconstructing attribution later, and TKT-222 has nothing to list without it.

success.note: Deterministic: signed-in checkout stores the customer, guest checkout stores NULL, a forged attribution is refused.

binding.rule: Money is integer minor units + ISO currency code - floats are banned on money paths.

Local gate: `make check` (lint + test + build, Go & TS, plus the gateway smoke suite; run `make deps` first on a clean clone). CI runs the same gate - keep them mirrored. Commit regenerated code (`openapi_gen.go`, `api-types.gen.ts`) before running the gate - `check-generate` diffs against HEAD, so an uncommitted regen reads as drift and fails the run.

A web-UI ticket isn't verified until a browser has *submitted* its forms. `make check`'s smoke suite exercises the catalog API directly and only *renders* back-office pages - it never submits an Astro form, so the whole class of "the SSR layer rejects/mangles the request before the handler runs" (CSRF/`checkOrigin`, base-path rewrites, redirects, CSP) is invisible to it.

governingAdrs.why: Cuts the system at five services + a stateless gateway. Customer accounts must land inside an existing service or the deviation is recorded as an ADR - ADR-042 rejected a sixth identity service and rejected giving the gateway a database.

The precedent AND its reasoning: staff accounts in catalog because catalog owns organizers; the SSR app owns the session, not the service; sessions in-process and unpersisted; per-principal session cap is what bounds the map; the cookie is path-scoped because storefront/scanner/admin/api share ONE origin. It also records that Astro's `security.checkOrigin` CANNOT be turned on behind the gateway (the Node adapter compares against the container Host) - a proxy-aware origin check replaces it.

The rule for where a guard lives: declared `security:` guards operations in a service's PUBLIC contract; an inline `X-Internal-Token` check guards its INTERNAL surface. Commerce's 404-on-internal is load-bearing (it matches the gateway edge-deny), not cargo. Whichever surface customer register/authenticate lands on, this decides how it is guarded.
Contract-first: any new operation is declared in the service's openapi.yaml and the generated code is committed before the gate runs.
Migrations run OUT-OF-BAND - the binary's `migrate` subcommand as a one-shot Compose job the service waits on. The server path never migrates. Any new table follows this.

The checkout recovery state machine. `orders.status='refunded'` already means a compensated FAILED checkout - do not overload order status. Anything added to the checkout path must not perturb the recovery states.

`guest_order_ref` is a BEARER credential for the ticket bundle (`/api/access/orders/{ref}/tickets` needs nothing else) and is never logged - TKT-202 is an open bug where the gateway logs it. Anything that surfaces or accepts an order ref inherits both properties.

Name the adversary before claiming a security property. 'A customer cannot see another customer's orders' means an unauthenticated or differently-authenticated HTTP caller - it says nothing about anyone with database access.
Response drift fails closed: a handler whose response does not match the declared schema is refused, so a new operation's schema must actually match what the handler writes.

reference.summary: BLAST RADIUS - `INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN` (compose.yaml `&go-env` anchor) is ONE shared value across all five Go services: whatever holds it can call commerce's /internal/orders/{id}/refunds, inventory's /internal/operational-holds and /internal/slots/{id}/capacity-adjustments, and access's refund surface. The storefront must NEVER receive it.
BLAST RADIUS - `COMMERCE_STAFF_WRITE_TOKEN` opens commerce's staff refund (money-moving). Held today only by the back office. The storefront must NEVER receive it.

The storefront container today has exactly ONE env var: `GATEWAY_URL`. It holds no credential of any kind and serves anonymous internet traffic. Any design that hands it a token is a new trust decision that must be argued, not assumed.

Precedent to mirror, not to copy blindly: staff sign-in is catalog `staff_accounts` (migration 0015, bcrypt + tripwire CHECK + non-empty-Down refusal), `services/catalog/internal/store/staff.go`, `services/catalog/internal/api/staff.go`; the SESSION lives in the back-office Astro process (`web/backoffice/src/lib/session.ts`, `gate.ts`, `src/middleware.ts`) - opaque 256-bit token, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, absolute 8h TTL, per-principal cap of 5, cookie scoped to `/admin` NOT `/`.

The checkout write that already exists and that this ticket extends: `services/commerce/internal/store/store.go` sets `orders.status='completed'` and mints `guest_order_ref` under a `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on the order row. Attribution goes in that transaction.
